video_title: The All-Alpha Sixers Are Still Figuring Things Out | Rachel Nichols & Chris Mannix

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: 76ers face early-season learning curve with new stars
quotes.excerpt: there's a learning curve for a team that is incorporating two new alphas into this group
quotes.quote: I anticipated the 76ers starting off slow. They are three and one now, I thought they would be one and three, just because there's a learning curve for a team that is incorporating two new alphas into this group in LeBron James and Jaylen Brown.

quotes.speaker: Rachel Nichols
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James's impact on team chemistry and performance
quotes.excerpt: he's just such a chemistry changer. He gets dropped in the pot, your entire recipe changes
quotes.quote: I think they should be very happy. Especially with LeBron James, because he's just such a chemistry changer. He gets dropped in the pot, your entire recipe changes. If you look at teams LeBron has gone to and gotten started at, it's always been a little uncertain at the beginning and people figuring out their roles. This has frankly gone better record-wise, numbers-wise, than in his last couple stops in terms of a start.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.excerpt: they're bottom third in the league in three-point makes and that was projected to be an issue
quotes.quote: There are some flashing yellow lights maybe with this team. One is the three-point shooting. They're bottom third in the league in three-point makes and that was projected to be an issue for this team coming into the season. LeBron James is basically an inside the three-point line guy now, Jaylen Brown is an inside the three-point line guy now. Joel Embiid can shoot threes, but you don't want him shooting threes, you want him exploiting mismatches in the post or making mid-range jumpers at the high post. They're not a great three-point shooting team and will that cost them if they can't get into the middle of the pack, close to the top ten in three-point percentage? And rebounding, that's a problem for this group.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Torian Prince's viral explanation of what constitutes a rebound
quotes.excerpt: you go up and grab the ball off the rim when it comes off. And then you grab it with two hands

text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: I saw a clip of LeBron James basically saying, who was he paraphrasing somebody saying, just jump up in the air.

text_blocks.speaker: Torian Prince
text_blocks.text: You go up and grab the ball off the rim when it comes off. And then you grab it with two hands. And you come down with it and that's considered a rebound. So they got more of those than we did.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.excerpt: when Joel Embiid is off the floor, they've got real problems when it comes to rebounding the basketball
quotes.quote: They lost Ariel Hukporti for the season with that Achilles tear. Adem Bona is okay, but when Joel Embiid is off the floor, they've got real problems when it comes to rebounding the basketball. If they don't get better contributions from their backup bigs, that's something that could rear its head as problematic, especially as they go up against these big teams that are out there.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Thunder's potential availability of Isaiah Hartenstein
quotes.excerpt: would the Thunder make Isaiah Hartenstein available, given that Aday Mara looks like he's ready to play?
quotes.quote: I wonder, to briefly pivot back to Oklahoma City, would the Thunder make Isaiah Hartenstein available, given that Aday Mara looks like he's ready to play? Because Aday Mara is ready to play. The guy's legit. And if you're looking around saying, Isaiah Hartenstein is available, don't you think New York is going to pick him up?

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown's reaction to being traded to the 76ers
quotes.excerpt: he was shocked when they traded Jaylen Brown and nobody told him, didn't see it coming
quotes.quote: There was a clip that was out there, I think it was on Bleacher Report, of the YouTube series that Jayson Tatum did. They clipped it of him saying like he was shocked when they traded Jaylen Brown and nobody told him, didn't see it coming, blah, blah, blah. And Jaylen Brown right afterwards, after I think they beat the Knicks, right in the season opener, he goes on social media and puts a cap out there, basically calling Jayson Tatum a liar.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Jayson Tatum's role in the Jaylen Brown trade
quotes.excerpt: not that Jayson Tatum asked for him to be traded, but that Jayson Tatum could have stopped it
quotes.quote: I believe that Jaylen Brown believes that not that Jayson Tatum asked for him to be traded, but that Jayson Tatum could have stopped it. That's what I believe. Not reporting that, that's just kind of my read of the tea leaves that's out there. That Jayson Tatum as the face of the franchise, if he wanted to stop this deal from going down, he could have, and he didn't do it.
